newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China's refiners request halt of 1Q diesel imports.
newsitem.headline: China's refiners request halt of 1Q diesel imports.

text.p: High diesel stocks in China have prompted domestic refiners to ask Beijing to stop issuing first quarter import licenses, Chinese trade sources said on Thursday.

"Yes, refiners have asked the State Planning Commission to stop issuing first quarter import licences about two weeks ago, but state planners have not yet granted any approval for the request," said a Chinese source at state refiner Sinopec.
"China's demand is very scattered currently," he said.
But Chinese trade sources said state planners in Beijing were unlikely to grant the approval as inventories in China, while high, had not reached critical levels.

"We are already approaching the end of the first quarter. Most imports for March have already been done. It is quite futile to do so now", an official at state trader Sinochem said of the refiners' appeal to halt imports.
"The situation is not so bad. Recent heavy imports have not caused any port congestions. It is just that inventories are high and domestic production have edged up marginally," he said.
State planners in Beijing could not be reached for comment.
Starting from December, China is estimated to have imported a total of two million tonnes of diesel to stock up ahead of the Chinese New Year in February, Chinese sources said.
"After the last buying spree, domestic inventories are high and recent Chinese imports have slowed," a trader in Singapore said.
